answer: Yes. The story uses sustained, layered metaphors to illuminate class, affection, and belonging. Kindness flowing “downhill, toward the people gravity was already working on” connects compassion with economic disadvantage, while the compliment kept like “a foreign coin” captures Denise’s uncertain entry into an unfamiliar social world. Recurring images—the torn blouse, jars, and Miss Emily’s remarks arriving “like weather”—gain new meanings as the relationships develop. The idiom of “having a spine” is also deftly extended through Daniel supposedly borrowing Denise’s, blending humor with insight into the family’s power dynamics.
